docs.description: Compact label for status, category, or user-entered content. 45 variants: type (status, icon-only, icon+text, closable, text-only) × status (success, neutral, warning, danger, info) × invert × show icon-leading. type=status for read-only state (Active, Pending); type=closable for user-entered tokens with ×; type=icon-only for pure glyph tags. Keep text to 1–3 words.

type.reason: Owner decision, 2026-09-23: Tag's type follows from content. The status dot is `indicator`, a close button `onClose`, an icon gives icon+text, or icon-only without words, and words alone are text-only; so the type is no prop the caller could set against its content.

rules.reason: Bespoke on both: a pill drawn from Figma's layers with the shared helpers, its close button a pressable of its own. MUI's Chip and Flutter's Chip each lay out a label, an avatar or icon and a delete icon with paddings and heights of their own, which fight Figma's five layouts; Tag is a label, not a control, so they bring nothing else.
As its width.
An inverted tag's close button is icon.sm, 16px, in every status, where every other close button is icon.xs: the larger target on the stronger fill, with less padding beside it.
An icon-only tag centres its icon; every other type starts from its leading part.
Each type lays its parts out its own way: the status dot sits inset.xs from its words, an icon or the close button inset.2xs, and an icon-only tag has one part and no gap.
The side with a dot or an icon is padded inset.xs, a side with words inset.sm, and an icon-only tag not at all: it is a square.
As the left: inset.sm beside words, inset.xs beside the close button, and inset.2xs beside an inverted tag's larger close button, in every status.
An icon-only tag is a fixed square; every other type hugs its words.
Same value, governed token; the icon's height is already bound to it ("icon size tracks text size").

Figma draws no inverted status tag: its dot is the status's strong colour, which is the inverted tag's fill, so it would not show. The shells refuse an inverted tag with a dot (the React types, and an assert in Flutter), as Button Group's refuse the vertical full-width group Figma does not draw.
The icon of an icon+text tag is the caller's: Figma draws the Icon/None placeholder and records no prop.
